name: Cytotoxic T cell (CD8)
short_description: Killer cell: spots infected or tumour cells by their MHC-I signal and kills them precisely with perforin and granzymes.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; nearly monochrome beige/grey palette — heterochromatin, mitochondria, Golgi and granules all read as the same dusty tone, violating the 'every structure must be a clearly distinct colour' rule; two ribosome dots also fused into a figure-eight shape)
textbook.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; colour separation still too muted/washed out between adjacent organelles, re-rendered for stronger legend-accurate colour coding)
textbook.3: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; nucleus clearly dominates the cell with only a thin cream-tan cytoplasm rim, slate-indigo heterochromatin clumped at the nuclear periphery around a pale peach nucleolus, seafoam mitochondria, apricot-orange Golgi stack, grey-blue centriole pair, dusty plum-maroon cytotoxic granule cluster and fine microvilli fringe all individually distinct colours per the house legend; thin clean outlines, dark charcoal background, no baked text/border)

sem.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; cell far too small within the frame and surface texture too sparse/wispy, doesn't fill the composition or convincingly read as a dense microvillus surface)
sem.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; improved density but surface texture still reads more like a smooth fuzzy ball than the branching ridge-and-microvilli texture of a real T-cell SEM)
sem.3: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; single round lymphocyte filling the frame, densely covered in fine branching microvilli/membrane-ridge texture, cool blue-to-violet surface with pale gold highlights on raised ridges, clean dark navy background, closely matches the real NIAID 'Healthy Human T Cell' reference's texture and palette; no text/scale bar/border)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; nucleus proportion smaller than required relative to a thick cytoplasm band, and colour palette trended toward washed-out pastel rather than natural biological tones)
3d.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; natural biological tints — warm peach-tan translucent cytoplasm, soft violet nucleus with dark clumped heterochromatin and a small peach nucleolus, seafoam mitochondria, orange Golgi stack, pale blue centriole pair, dense plum-red cytotoxic granule cluster polarised to one side, fine microvilli fringe with soft rim light on a clean dark studio background; structures individually readable for labelling, no border/text)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; hand-painted naturalist-plate look, warm aged paper fills the frame edge-to-edge with a soft darker wash halo directly behind the single centred specimen, nucleus dominates with fine ink hatching for heterochromatin and a small red nucleolus, mitochondria/Golgi/granules/centrioles all rendered as distinct washes with fine ink linework and a stippled ribosome scatter, fine ink microvilli fringe; no mat/frame/drop-shadow, no baked text)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Healthy Human T Cell.jpg", NIAID/NIH, Public Domain — colorized SEM of a single isolated human T lymphocyte showing the characteristic dense, ruffled microvillus surface; clean dark background, no baked-in text/scale bar/border; used as-is, no cleaning edit needed. Note: CD4 vs CD8 T cells are not visually distinguishable by shape alone under EM/light microscopy — a 'T lymphocyte' micrograph is the standard honest reference for this cell.)
